U16-C06-REWARD.editorial_treatment: Documented correction C06, with exact source prompt and primary evidence preserved separately.
U16-C06-REWARD.inspection_scope: The printed weak headword/class belong to a verb meaning sin or fail in duty. Repay/reward requires the distinct strong gyldan verb. The source English, original hint and original image are all retained; only modern guidance is corrected.

supporting_primary_evidence.observation: Strong a-gildan/-geldan/-gieldan/-gyldan has geald/guldon/golden and includes reward, repay, requite. Separate weak a-giltan has gilte/gilt and means sin, fail, do wrong.
a-gyldan expressly gives thu gyltst/he gylt and geald/guldon/golden. Dative recipients occur in repayment examples. Separate a-gyltan/-giltan has gylte/gilte and gylt/gilt, fail in duty or sin.
Reward is the noun med; requite is forgieldan(III.104). The vocabulary supplies no independent support for agyltan as the verb reward.
Strong gieldan/geald/guldon/golden is explicitly tabulated under104. Prefixing does not turn this into weak class113.
Section113 describes weak de/te preterits retaining the stem vowel, with hieran, fyllan, cyssan, settan and sendan among its examples. It cannot describe strong gyldan/geald/guldon/golden.

additional_primary_corroboration.original_identifier: Matthew16.27, left/first column and its A apparatus
additional_primary_corroboration.observation: Leftcolumn prints mannes Sunu ys to cumenne and then agylt æghwylcum be hys agenum worce. Apparatus at bottom explicitly gives Ch.xvi.v.27,6.A.cumanne and21.A.B.weorce. This corroborates the bounded impending-coming phrase, selected cumanne variant, contracted reward verb and dative recipient. The new model is not presented as an exact quotation of this differently spelled parallel.

U16-LATIN-NOTE10.editorial_treatment: Modern English support for exact source apparatus; no Old English emendation.
U16-LATIN-NOTE10.inspection_scope: Latin ceroma fricavit eum means rubbing/anointing him with ointment; the printed Latin contains no explicit shoulder or neck noun. Do not introduce either as a certain literal gloss.

lexical_confirmation.source: Lewis and Short, ceroma; Georges, ceroma
lexical_confirmation.finding: Ointment used by wrestlers; Georges includes feminine first-declension ceroma, ae and cites Historia Apollonii13.

U16-LATIN-NOTE10.teaching_boundary: Supply an English sense of both Latin parallels; assume no prior Latin. Preserve Cook’s tentative ball interpretation of Old English top and its acknowledged divergence.

U16-MT-P114.inspection_scope: Firstcolumn14.8: Iohannes heafod þæs fulluhteres. Firstcolumn14.10: beheafdode Iohannem on þam cwerterne. The genitive Iohannes and accusative Iohannem are directly attested; the rightcolumn variant Iohanne is not silently substituted.
U16-MT-P114.declared_normalization: Retain the attested endings, writing initial J in Johannes/Johannem solely to follow Cook’s printed Johannes hint. No vowel quantity is inferred and no complete Latin proper-name system is assigned.
U16-MT-P114.teaching_scope: Supply Johannes as the genitive in36.9 and Johannem as the accusative in36.10; identify both roles explicitly.
